You are a subagent spawned by another session.
Implement Phase E4 (Plan Engine: goal math + backup levers) of the Financial Resilience Engine in "/Users/ajeet/Projects/Hackathons/Sheridan Datathon 2026", following the approved tech-lead design below exactly. E1-E3 are complete and committed. React 19 / Vite 6 / TS 5.7 strict / Tailwind 3.4 / Vitest; Python 3.14 + uv + pytest.

## Staged delivery protocol (mandatory)
Write and test in stages; each stage's files must be ON DISK with green targeted tests before the next begins. Never hold multiple stages in memory.
Stage 1: planMath.ts additions + unit goldens/invariants. Stage 2: golden_plans.json + planMath.golden.test.ts. Stage 3: planText.ts + PlanCard.tsx + index.css + tests. Stage 4: Python twin (shocks.py scale_cents, plans.py finish, test_plans.py). Stage 5: dashScan registration + full gates.

## Hard constraints
- Integer cents throughout; no float decides a branch. Runway math ONLY via shocks.runway (every lever "+N months" = difference of two shocks.runway answers; acceptance check includes grepping for any other runway formula in planMath/planText).
- No em/en dashes, minus sign equivalents, double or spaced hyphens in ANY new string or comment (numeric minus in formatted money allowed).
- ZERO diff to src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx and src/state/consoleStore.ts (E3 just landed there; the only seam is the existing <PlanCard plan={derivation.plan} /> call site, which must remain byte-identical).
- Do NOT touch: weather/, forecast, shockParse, TypedShock, ShockChips, atlas/, judge/, stormAtlas, judgeMode, scripts/engine/verify.py or build.py, public/data/engine/ (except the new golden_plans.json which lives in scripts/engine/).

## User-confirmed decisions
1. Months-to-goal counts new contributions from zero (preserves E2 invariant) + printed disclosure line "Savings on hand: $B (x.x months of spending), not counted in the months above."
2. RESTORE scripts/engine/plans.py as a test-side Python twin (no build/verify coupling): add scale_cents to scripts/engine/shocks.py (fixes the dormant broken import), finish plans.py goal/backup/levers, new scripts/engine/test_plans.py, new shared frozen scripts/engine/golden_plans.json asserted by BOTH vitest and pytest.
3. Insurance lever = full median insurance_cents, labeled "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation", available only when insurance > 0 (unit-test synthetically; fixtures have 0).
4. Lever ladder order: shop_insurance → trim_discretionary → defer_loan (free moves first), applied cumulatively.

## Design spec

### src/lib/planMath.ts (extend; goalPlan/backupPlan stay byte-stable)
Add: GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6 (beside existing GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3); GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6]; GoalMilestone {monthsOfSpending, amountCents, monthsToReach, isGoal, isStretch} + goalMilestones(incomeCents, spendingCents); LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'; LeverEffect {incomeDeltaCents, spendingDeltaCents, bufferDeltaCents} (all E4 levers: income 0, buffer 0, spending <= 0); Lever {id, label, caveat, effect}; LeverInputs {shockedIncomeCents, shockedSpendingCents, oneOffCents, bufferCents (profile.buffer_cents pre one-off), fixedCostsCents (F), loanPaymentCents (P), insuranceCents, typicalSpendingCents (S)}; LeverStep {lever, incomeAfterCents, spendingAfterCents, bufferLeftCents, runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer, plusDeciMonths, stepDeciMonths}; LeverLadder {baseline, steps}; leverLadder(input).

Lever semantics:
| Order | id | Availability | Effect | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | shop_insurance | insuranceCents > 0 | spendingDelta = -insuranceCents | "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation" |
| 2 | trim_discretionary | disc = max(0, S - (F+P)) > 0 | spendingDelta = -disc | "simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed" |
| 3 | defer_loan | loanPaymentCents > 0 | spendingDelta = -loanPaymentCents | "simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled" |
Composition: filter to available levers in order, apply cumulatively (spendingAfter = max(0, shockedSpending + Σ deltas), defensive guard asserted unreachable on fixtures), and per step re-run shocks.runway(bufferCents, oneOffCents, shockedIncome, spendingAfter). Levers are sized from PROFILE numbers (judge part-1 metrics), never shocked ones.
Display rules for +N (in planText, dash clean): both finite → "+X.X months"; baseline finite → after no_shortfall → "clears the shortfall (120+ months)"; baseline buffer_depleted → "+0.0 months (buffer depleted: restore a positive balance first)".

### src/lib/planText.ts (extend; signature buildPlanText(profile, result, twist, band) unchanged)
PlanText grows: goalChips: GoalChip[] {label, amountCents, monthsToReach, highlight: 'goal'|'stretch'|'plain'}; levers: LeverRow[] {id, label, caveat, effectCents, runwayAfter (formatted), plusLabel, plusDeciMonths, stepDeciMonths}; definitions: string[]. Delegate goal numbers to goalPlan/goalMilestones (remove inline cushion math). Definition strip (5 lines, exact content from design): starter cushion 3x S definition; contribution = max(income minus spending, 5 percent of income); months to target from zero + savings-on-hand line; backup horizon 6 months matching the EI twist; cut floor is F plus P with the note that labeled levers may go under it on purpose.
APPROVED STRING CHURN (document in planText.test.ts header so review doesn't read it as breakage): the deficit goal line is replaced by the cut-needed story from goalPlan; new chip/lever/definition fields appear.

### src/components/console/PlanCard.tsx (extend) + src/index.css
Render chips row, lever table (label, effect, runwayAfter, +N), definitions strip. Still strings + formatCents/formatDeciMonths only, zero math. Update the docstring claiming plans are E2 templates.

### Shared goldens: scripts/engine/golden_plans.json (NEW, frozen after review)
5 fixture accounts under the standard COMBO twist (job loss EI 55%, bills +15%), with visible workings (steps strings), matching golden_fixtures.json style. Verified hand-computed numbers (deci = tenths of a month):
- 68257: shocked 357679/780685/finite 15. Ladder: trim -919 → 779766, finite 15, +0; defer -284493 → 495273, finite 47, +32. Backup: floor 715165, survives no, shortfall 45.
- 23838: shocked 154222/192913/finite 835. Ladder: trim -46227 → 146686, no_shortfall 1200, +365. Backup: floor 127553, yes, 0.
- 49900: shocked 0/6293/finite 1200 (cap). Ladder: trim -6293 → 0, no_shortfall 1200, +0. Backup: floor 0, yes, 0.
- 98952: shocked 215336/446037/finite 38. Ladder: trim -302969 → 143068, no_shortfall 1200, +1162. Backup: floor 124407, no, 22.
- 42988: shocked 791562/1687955/buffer_depleted 0. Ladder: trim -386907 → 1301048, buffer_depleted 0, +0; defer -473085 → 827963, buffer_depleted 0, +0. Backup: floor 1206185, no, 60.
Goal goldens (twist independent): 68257 target 2148252 contribution 32516 months 67 cut 98274 "cut needed" chips 23/45/67/133; 23838 target 521340 contribution 106623 months 5 cut 0 "on track" chips 2/4/5/10; 49900 "needs income" (months/cut -1) chips all -1; 98952 target 1282128 contribution 19576 months 66 cut 55432 chips 22/44/66/131; 42988 target 4779276 contribution 71960 months 67 cut 225849 chips 23/45/67/133. Invariant: k=3 chip monthsToReach equals goalPlan.months on every account.

### Tests
- planMath.test.ts (extend): full ladder synthetic golden (ins 30000, P 50000, disc 150000, IDLE, B 2000000, I 300000, S 400000, F 200000: baseline finite 200; step1 → spending 370000 finite 286 +86; step2 → 220000 no_shortfall 1200 +1000; step3 → 170000 no_shortfall +1000 marginal 0); S < F+P disc clamp; negative buffer all steps 0; availability matrix. Invariants: monotonicity (plus >= 0, step >= 0, runwayAfter >= baseline) over fixtures + integer grid; cumulative == sequential (final row equals single runway over summed effects); Number.isInteger on all exported money/month fields.
- planMath.golden.test.ts (new): reads golden_plans.json + golden_fixtures.json, builds via applyTwist (mirror shocks.golden.test.ts construction), asserts every number above.
- planText.test.ts (extend): approved churn documented in header; chips/lever/definition assertions; 98952 cap-crossing label reads "clears the shortfall (120+ months)"; dash sweep over new fields.
- PlanCard render test: chips, lever rows, definitions appear; zero math (string assertions).
- Python: scripts/engine/shocks.py scale_cents(base_cents, pct) = round_half_up(base*pct, 100); scripts/engine/plans.py finish (goal_milestones, lever_ladder scalar, fix the scale_cents call arity, replace the DEFERRED header); scripts/engine/test_plans.py asserting golden_plans.json + mirrored unit cases + invariants.
- dashScan.test.ts: register planMath.ts, planMath.test.ts, planMath.golden.test.ts (planText/PlanCard already covered via existing registration; verify).

## Verification (all must pass; report each)
1. npx vitest run (full: 426 existing must stay green + new)
2. npm run typecheck; 3. npm run build
4. uv run pytest -q (130 existing + new test_plans)
5. uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify (PASS, artifact unchanged)
6. git diff HEAD -- src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx src/state/consoleStore.ts must be EMPTY
7. Grep proof: no runway formula other than shocks.runway calls in planMath/planText.

If you need clarification or encounter ambiguity, output your questions in this exact format at the TOP of your response:

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: [your question]

Then continue with your best-effort output based on available information.

Report: files per stage, golden parity results (TS + Python), invariant results, gate outputs, ConsoleView/store zero-diff proof, deviations with rationale.

<skill_content name="frontend-design">
# Skill: frontend-design

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.

## Ground it in the subject

If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.

Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again

For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. # Skill: frontend-design

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.

## Ground it in the subject

If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.

Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again

For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

6: /**
7:  * Goal and backup plan text for one account under one twist: plain
8:  * sentences built from the same integer cents the verdict reads, so the
9:  * card a judge quotes matches the numbers on screen to the cent. All
10:  * arithmetic happens here (never in a component), and the templates stay
11:  * honest and simple in Phase E2: a starter cushion goal, a surplus or
12:  * deficit statement, then the baseline versus shocked runway, the shocked
13:  * monthly gap, and the horizon check. The backup levers with +N month
14:  * effects are Phase E4 (docs/architecture.md).
15:  */
16: 
17: export interface PlanText {
18:   /** Goal block: build the emergency fund from this account's own numbers. */
19:   goal: string[]
20:   /** Backup block: what the shock does and whether the buffer rides it out. */
21:   backup: string[]
22: }
23: 
24: /** Months of typical spending the starter cushion targets. */
25: export const CUSHION_MONTHS = 3
26: 
27: /**
28:  * Build the two plan blocks for one profile under one twist.
29:  *
30:  * profile supplies the baseline (I, S, B and the recorded runway),
31:  * result supplies the shocked numbers, twist supplies the display only
32:  * horizon, and band names the shocked verdict inside the backup line so
33:  * the sentence and the badge cannot disagree.
34:  */
35: export function buildPlanText(
36:   profile: AccountProfile,
37:   result: ShockResult,
38:   twist: Twist,
39:   band: VerdictBand,
40: ): PlanText {
41:   const cushionCents = profile.spending_cents * CUSHION_MONTHS
42:   const surplusCents = profile.income_cents - profile.spending_cents
43: 
44:   const goal: string[] = [
45:     `Starter cushion: ${formatCents(cushionCents)} (${CUSHION_MONTHS} months of typical spending).`,
46:     surplusCents >= 0
47:       ? `Monthly surplus: ${formatCents(surplusCents)} (income minus spending).`
48:       : `Monthly deficit: ${formatCents(-surplusCents)} (spending exceeds income).`,
49:   ]
50: 
51:   if (surplusCents > 0) {
52:     const months = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(cushionCents / surplusCents))
53:     goal.push(
54:       `Setting aside ${formatCents(surplusCents)} a month builds the cushion in about ${months} months.`,
55:     )
56:   } else {
57:     goal.push('A monthly deficit means the cushion goal waits for income or spending to move.')
58:   }
59: 
60:   const baselineRunway = formatDeciMonths(profile.runway_deci_months, profile.runway_state)
61:   const shockedRunway = formatDeciMonths(result.runway.deciMonths, result.runway.state)
62: 
63:   const backup: string[] = [
64:     `Baseline steady state: ${baselineRunway}. Shocked steady state: ${shockedRunway} (${band.label}).`,
65:     result.gapAfterCents > 0
66:       ? `Monthly shortfall after the shock: ${formatCents(result.gapAfterCents)}.`
67:       : 'No monthly shortfall after the shock.',
68:   ]
69: 
70:   if (twist.durationMonths > 0) {
71:     const covers =
72:       result.runway.state === 'no_shortfall' ||
73:       result.runway.deciMonths >= twist.durationMonths * 10
74:     backup.push(
75:       covers
76:         ? `The shocked runway covers the ${twist.durationMonths} month horizon.`
77:         : `The shocked runway runs out before the ${twist.durationMonths} month horizon ends.`,
78:     )
79:   }
80: 
81:   return { goal, backup }
82: }

132:     return fallback
133:   }
134:   const clamped = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, value))
135:   // Quantize to hundredths so a slider value and a preset value compare
136:   // equal after one rounding step (0.55 stays 0.55, 0.5549 becomes 0.55).
137:   return Math.round(clamped * 100) / 100
138: }
139: 
140: /**
141:  * Clamp and quantize a twist to the fields the math accepts. Missing
142:  * fields fall back to IDLE_TWIST, so a preset can declare only the fields
143:  * it changes. This is the only place slider input becomes math input.
144:  */
145: export function normalizeTwist(twist: Partial<Twist>): Twist {
146:   const base = { ...IDLE_TWIST, ...twist }
147:   return {
148:     jobLoss: base.jobLoss === true,
149:     incomeFactor: clampFactor(base.incomeFactor, IDLE_TWIST.incomeFactor),
150:     billsDeltaPct: clampInt(base.billsDeltaPct, 0, 100, IDLE_TWIST.billsDeltaPct),
151:     oneOffMonthsTenths: clampInt(base.oneOffMonthsTenths, 0, 30, IDLE_TWIST.oneOffMonthsTenths),
152:     extraMonthlyCents: clampInt(
153:       base.extraMonthlyCents,
154:       0,
155:       MAX_EXTRA_MONTHLY_CENTS,
156:       IDLE_TWIST.extraMonthlyCents,
157:     ),
158:     durationMonths: clampInt(
159:       base.durationMonths,
160:       0,
161:       MAX_DURATION_MONTHS,
162:       IDLE_TWIST.durationMonths,
163:     ),
164:   }
165: }
166: 
167: /** Field by field twist equality, used to recognize an untouched preset. */
168: export function sameTwist(left: Twist, right: Twist): boolean {
169:   return (
170:     left.jobLoss === right.jobLoss &&
171:     left.incomeFactor === right.incomeFactor &&
172:     left.billsDeltaPct === right.billsDeltaPct &&
173:     left.oneOffMonthsTenths === right.oneOffMonthsTenths &&
174:     left.extraMonthlyCents === right.extraMonthlyCents &&

176:   )
177: }

180:  * Unit conversions between what a slider holds and what the math holds.
181:  * Views call these instead of doing arithmetic in JSX: the console shows
182:  * income as a percent and one off cost as months of spending, while the
183:  * math keeps incomeFactor as a fraction and oneOffMonthsTenths as tenths.
184:  */
185: export function factorToPercent(factor: number): number {
186:   return Math.round(factor * 100)
187: }
188: 
189: export function percentToFactor(percent: number): number {
190:   return percent / 100
191: }
192: 
193: export function tenthsToMonths(tenths: number): number {
194:   return tenths / 10
195: }
196: 
197: export function monthsToTenths(months: number): number {
198:   return Math.round(months * 10)
199: }
200: 
201: /** Every number a shocked card shows, all integer cents plus the runway. */
202: export interface ShockResult {
203:   /** I after the twist (unchanged when jobLoss is false). */
204:   incomeAfterCents: number
205:   /** S after bills increase and recurring extra cost, one off excluded. */
206:   spendingAfterCents: number
207:   /** One off cost subtracted from the buffer only, never from spending. */
208:   oneOffCents: number
209:   /** B minus the one off cost. */
210:   bufferLeftCents: number
211:   /** spendingAfter minus incomeAfter. */
212:   gapAfterCents: number
213:   /** The judge runway over the shocked numbers. */
214:   runway: RunwayAnswer

217: /**
218:  * Apply one twist to one profile. The one off semantics follow the
219:  * challenge doc exactly: one off costs subtract from the buffer only,
220:  * billsDeltaPct adds scaleCents(H, pct) to spending, extraMonthlyCents is
221:  * recurring spending, and income becomes scaleCents(I, eiPct) only when
222:  * the job is lost. The twist is normalized first so no caller can feed
223:  * the branch math an out of range value.

226:   const normalized = normalizeTwist(twist)

229:   const incomeAfterCents = normalized.jobLoss

1: """The judge runway formula as one pure function in integer cents.
2: 
3: Runway (months) from docs/tangerine-challenge.md, branch order exact:
4: 
5:     buffer_left = B - one_off_costs
6:     gap         = spending_after_shock - income_after_shock
7:     if buffer_left <= 0:  state = buffer_depleted, deci_months = 0
8:     elif gap <= 0:        state = no_shortfall,    deci_months = 1200
9:     else:                 state = finite, deci_months = half up
10:                             (10 * buffer_left / gap), capped at 1200
11: 
12: The finite branch is exact integer arithmetic:
13: deci_months = (20 * buffer_left + gap) // (2 * gap) for positive
14: operands, which equals ROUND_HALF_UP(10 * buffer_left / gap), then
15: min(1200). No float can flip a branch or drift between build, verify,
16: and tests. deci_months is tenths of a month: 1200 means 120 months.
17: 
18: Run from the repository root:
19: 
20:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
21: """
22:

24: 
25: from dataclasses import dataclass
26: from typing import Literal

28: RunwayState = Literal["finite", "no_shortfall", "buffer_depleted"]

45:     income_cents: int,

47: ) -> Runway:
48:     """Judge runway for one account, all values integer cents.
49: 
50:     income_cents and spending_cents are the post shock values; the
51:     baseline runway passes I and S unchanged with one_off_cents = 0.

53:     buffer_left = buffer_cents - one_off_cents
54:     gap = spending_cents - income_cents

1: """Goal plan and backup plan, the engine's own definitions.
2: 
3: DEFERRED TO PHASE E4: the E1 profile precompute does not use this
4: module. The draft below stays importable and tested by nothing yet so
5: Phase E4 can finish it against the profiles.json contract in
6: docs/profiles-schema.md; the E1 build writes goal and backup plans
7: nowhere.
8: 
9: The brief allows our own definitions as long as we can explain them. Both
10: plans are pure functions of the judge metrics, computed in integer cents:
11: 
12: Goal plan (emergency fund):
13: * target = 3 times typical spending S (three months of runway money)
14: * monthly contribution = max(I - S, 5 percent of I), the pay yourself first
15:   floor when income does not exceed spending
16: * months to goal = ceil(target / contribution)
17: * when I <= S the plan also states the exact monthly cut needed to make the
18:   goal reachable: cut = S - I + contribution, the amount that turns the
19:   forced floor into a real surplus. When contribution is 0 (no income) the
20:   plan reports the goal as unreachable until income starts.
21: 
22: Backup plan:
23: * runway under the standard EI twist (job loss, EI at 55 percent) judged
24:   against a stated horizon of 6 months, matching the brief's EI duration
25: * the cut floor is fixed costs F plus loan payment P: those are the bills
26:   that cannot be cut away, named so the plan never suggests skipping them
27: 
28: Run from the repository root:
29: 
30:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
31: """
32: 
33: from __future__ import annotations
34: 
35: import numpy as np
36: 
37: from scripts.engine.shocks import scale_cents
38: 
39: GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS: int = 3
40: GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT: int = 5
41: BACKUP_HORIZON_MONTHS: int = 6
42: BACKUP_SCENARIO_LABEL: str = "job loss, EI at 55 percent for 6 months"
43: 
44: # Sentinel arrays use these for values that publish as JSON null: a goal
45: # with no contribution has no month count and no cut (it needs income).
46: MONTHS_UNREACHABLE: int = -1
47: CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE: int = -1
48: 
49: 
50: def goal_plans(
51:     income_cents: int | np.ndarray, spending_cents: int | np.ndarray
52: ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
53:     """Vectorized goal plans for every account at once.
54: 
55:     Returns target, contribution, months (or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE), and
56:     monthly cut (0 when no cut is needed, CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE when the goal
57:     needs income first), all integer cents except the month counts.
58:     """
59:     income = np.asarray(income_cents, dtype="int64")
60:     spending = np.asarray(spending_cents, dtype="int64")
61:     target = np.int64(GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS) * spending
62:     floor = np.asarray(
63:         scale_cents(income, GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT, 100), dtype="int64"
64:     )
65:     contribution = np.maximum(income - spending, floor)
66: 
67:     months = np.full(income.shape, MONTHS_UNREACHABLE, dtype="int64")
68:     funded = contribution > 0
69:     months[funded] = (
70:         target[funded] + contribution[funded] - np.int64(1)
71:     ) // contribution[funded]
72: 
73:     cut = np.zeros(income.shape, dtype="int64")
74:     needs_cut = (income <= spending) & funded
75:     cut[needs_cut] = spending[needs_cut] - income[needs_cut] + contribution[needs_cut]
76:     cut[~funded] = CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE
77: 
78:     return {
79:         "target": target,
80:         "contribution": contribution,
81:         "months": months,
82:         "cut": cut,
83:     }
84: 
85: 
86: def goal_status(
87:     income_cents: int | np.ndarray,
88:     contribution: int | np.ndarray,
89:     cut: int | np.ndarray,
90: ) -> np.ndarray:
91:     """Status string per account: needs income, cut needed, or on track."""
92:     income = np.asarray(income_cents, dtype="int64")
93:     contribution_array = np.asarray(contribution, dtype="int64")
94:     cut_array = np.asarray(cut, dtype="int64")
95:     status = np.full(income.shape, "on track", dtype=object)
96:     needs_cut = cut_array > 0
97:     status[needs_cut] = "cut needed"
98:     status[contribution_array <= 0] = "needs income"
99:     return status
100: 
101: 
102: def backup_plans(
103:     fixed_cents: int | np.ndarray,
104:     loan_cents: int | np.ndarray,
105:     state: np.ndarray,
106:     tenths: np.ndarray,
107:     horizon_months: int = BACKUP_HORIZON_MONTHS,
108: ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
109:     """Vectorized backup plans: horizon verdict plus the named cut floor.
110: 
111:     survives = no shortfall, or numeric runway at or beyond the horizon.
112:     shortfall_tenths is how far the runway falls under the horizon (0 when
113:     it clears), and cut_floor = F + P names what cannot be cut.
114:     """
115:     fixed = np.asarray(fixed_cents, dtype="int64")
116:     loan = np.asarray(loan_cents, dtype="int64")
117:     horizon_tenths = np.int64(horizon_months * 10)
118:     state_array = np.asarray(state, dtype=np.int8)
119:     tenths_array = np.asarray(tenths, dtype="int64")
120: 
121:     survives = (state_array == 1) | ((state_array == 2) & (tenths_array >= horizon_tenths))
122:     shortfall = np.zeros(state_array.shape, dtype="int64")
123:     zero_buffer = state_array == 0
124:     short_numeric = (state_array == 2) & (tenths_array < horizon_tenths)
125:     shortfall[zero_buffer] = horizon_tenths
126:     shortfall[short_numeric] = horizon_tenths - tenths_array[short_numeric]
127: 
128:     return {
129:         "cutFloor": fixed + loan,
130:         "survives": survives,
131:         "shortfallTenths": shortfall,
132:     }

16: * months to goal = ceil(target / contribution)
17: * when I <= S the plan also states the exact monthly cut needed to make the
18:   goal reachable: cut = S - I + contribution, the amount that turns the
19:   forced floor into a real surplus. When contribution is 0 (no income) the
20:   plan reports the goal as unreachable until income starts.
21: 
22: Backup plan:
23: * runway under the standard EI twist (job loss, EI at 55 percent) judged
24:   against a stated horizon of 6 months, matching the brief's EI duration
25: * the cut floor is fixed costs F plus loan payment P: those are the bills
26:   that cannot be cut away, named so the plan never suggests skipping them
27: 
28: Run from the repository root:
29: 
30:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
31: """
32: 
33: from __future__ import annotations
34: 
35: import numpy as np
36: 
37: from scripts.engine.shocks import scale_cents
38: 
39: GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS: int = 3
40: GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT: int = 5
41: BACKUP_HORIZON_MONTHS: int = 6
42: BACKUP_SCENARIO_LABEL: str = "job loss, EI at 55 percent for 6 months"
43: 
44: # Sentinel arrays use these for values that publish as JSON null: a goal
45: # with no contribution has no month count and no cut (it needs income).
46: MONTHS_UNREACHABLE: int = -1
47: CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE: int = -1
48: 
49: 
50: def goal_plans(
51:     income_cents: int | np.ndarray, spending_cents: int | np.ndarray
52: ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
53:     """Vectorized goal plans for every account at once.
54: 
55:     Returns target, contribution, months (or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE), and
56:     monthly cut (0 when no cut is needed, CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE when the goal
57:     needs income first), all integer cents except the month counts.
58:     """
59:     income = np.asarray(income_cents, dtype="int64")
60:     spending = np.asarray(spending_cents, dtype="int64")
61:     target = np.int64(GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS) * spending
62:     floor = np.asarray(
63:         scale_cents(income, GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT, 100), dtype="int64"
64:     )
65:     contribution = np.maximum(income - spending, floor)
66: 
67:     months = np.full(income.shape, MONTHS_UNREACHABLE, dtype="int64")
68:     funded = contribution > 0
69:     months[funded] = (
70:         target[funded] + contribution[funded] - np.int64(1)
71:     ) // contribution[funded]
72: 
73:     cut = np.zeros(income.shape, dtype="int64")
74:     needs_cut = (income <= spending) & funded
75:     cut[needs_cut] = spending[needs_cut] - income[needs_cut] + contribution[needs_cut]
76:     cut[~funded] = CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE
77: 
78:     return {
79:         "target": target,
80:         "contribution": contribution,
81:         "months": months,
82:         "cut": cut,
83:     }
84: 
85: 
86: def goal_status(
87:     income_cents: int | np.ndarray,
88:     contribution: int | np.ndarray,
89:     cut: int | np.ndarray,
90: ) -> np.ndarray:
91:     """Status string per account: needs income, cut needed, or on track."""
92:     income = np.asarray(income_cents, dtype="int64")
93:     contribution_array = np.asarray(contribution, dtype="int64")
94:     cut_array = np.asarray(cut, dtype="int64")
95:     status = np.full(income.shape, "on track", dtype=object)
96:     needs_cut = cut_array > 0
97:     status[needs_cut] = "cut needed"
98:     status[contribution_array <= 0] = "needs income"
99:     return status
100: 
101: 
102: def backup_plans(
103:     fixed_cents: int | np.ndarray,
104:     loan_cents: int | np.ndarray,
105:     state: np.ndarray,
106:     tenths: np.ndarray,
107:     horizon_months: int = BACKUP_HORIZON_MONTHS,
108: ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
109:     """Vectorized backup plans: horizon verdict plus the named cut floor.
110: 
111:     survives = no shortfall, or numeric runway at or beyond the horizon.
112:     shortfall_tenths is how far the runway falls under the horizon (0 when
113:     it clears), and cut_floor = F + P names what cannot be cut.
114:     """
115:     fixed = np.asarray(fixed_cents, dtype="int64")
116:     loan = np.asarray(loan_cents, dtype="int64")
117:     horizon_tenths = np.int64(horizon_months * 10)
118:     state_array = np.asarray(state, dtype=np.int8)
119:     tenths_array = np.asarray(tenths, dtype="int64")
120: 
121:     survives = (state_array == 1) | ((state_array == 2) & (tenths_array >= horizon_tenths))
122:     shortfall = np.zeros(state_array.shape, dtype="int64")
123:     zero_buffer = state_array == 0
124:     short_numeric = (state_array == 2) & (tenths_array < horizon_tenths)
125:     shortfall[zero_buffer] = horizon_tenths
126:     shortfall[short_numeric] = horizon_tenths - tenths_array[short_numeric]
127: 
128:     return {
129:         "cutFloor": fixed + loan,
130:         "survives": survives,
131:         "shortfallTenths": shortfall,
132:     }

1: """Pure judge metrics over integer cent row sequences.
2: 
3: Every function in this module is pure: no pandas, no numpy, no file IO.
4: All money values are integer CAD cents and rounding happens once at the
5: metric boundary with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero).
6: 
7: Judge definitions from docs/tangerine-challenge.md:
8: 
9: * I = median of money_in over all monthly rows
10: * F = median over months of the per month row sum household_bills +
11:   insurance + loan_payments (per row sums first, never a sum of medians)
12: * S = median of money_out over all monthly rows
13: * B = mean of avg_daily_balance over the last min(6, n) rows sorted by
14:   month, rounded half up; fewer than 6 rows uses every available row
15: * H = median of household_bills over all monthly rows
16: * P = monthly_payment from loans.csv when status is C or D (running at
17:   the end of 2025), otherwise 0; P comes from the loan record in build.py
18: * gap = S minus I
19: 
20: Run from the repository root:
21: 
22:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
23: """
24: 
25: from __future__ import annotations
26: 
27: from dataclasses import dataclass
28: from typing import Sequence
29: 
30: # Rule versions recorded in the artifact meta.
31: METRIC_RULE_VERSION: str = "judge-metrics-v1"
32: 
33: # The buffer window is the last 6 rows by month (the judge rule for B).
34: BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS: int = 6
35: 
36: # The thin_history flag threshold: fewer than 18 monthly rows, a quarter
37: # of the 72 month dataset span (2020-01 to 2025-12). Every real account
38: # has at least 12 rows, so a 6 row threshold would never fire; 18 fires
39: # on the genuinely short histories (rationale recorded in the Phase E1
40: # decision record, docs/decisions.md). The flag is separate from
41: # BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS, which only decides how many rows B averages.
42: THIN_HISTORY_ROWS: int = 18
43: 
44: # The single swappable rule deciding which loan statuses count as running
45: # at the end of 2025 (user confirmed decision, docs/decisions.md E1).
46: RUNNING_STATUS_RULE: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"C", "D"})
47: DEFAULTED_STATUS: str = "D"
48: END_OF_2025_MONTH: str = "2025-12"
49: 
50: 
51: @dataclass(frozen=True)
52: class RowCents:
53:     """One monthly_summary row with every money value in integer cents."""
54: 
55:     month: str
56:     money_in: int
57:     money_out: int
58:     household_bills: int
59:     insurance: int
60:     loan_payments: int
61:     pension_in: int
62:     avg_daily_balance: int
63: 
64: 
65: @dataclass(frozen=True)
66: class Metrics:
67:     """The six judge numbers plus the F decomposition and the gap."""
68: 
69:     income_cents: int
70:     fixed_costs_cents: int
71:     spending_cents: int
72:     buffer_cents: int
73:     household_bills_cents: int
74:     insurance_cents: int
75:     loan_payments_median_cents: int
76:     pension_in_cents: int
77:     gap_cents: int
78: 
79: 
80: def round_half_up(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> int:
81:     """Divide with ROUND_HALF_UP: ties away from zero (decimal semantics).
82: 
83:     The positive case is (numerator + denominator // 2) // denominator;
84:     the sign split makes negative operands round away from zero on ties
85:     as well, which matches Python's decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.
86:     """
87:     if denominator <= 0:
88:         raise ValueError(f"denominator must be positive, got {denominator}")
89:     sign = 1 if numerator >= 0 else -1
90:     magnitude = (abs(numerator) + denominator // 2) // denominator
91:     return sign * magnitude
92: 
93: 
94: def median_cents(values: Sequence[int]) -> int:
95:     """Median of integer cents: middle value, or half up mean of two middles."""
96:     if not values:
97:         raise ValueError("median_cents requires at least one value")
98:     ordered = sorted(values)
99:     middle = len(ordered) // 2
100:     if len(ordered) % 2 == 1:
101:         return ordered[middle]
102:     return round_half_up(ordered[middle - 1] + ordered[middle], 2)
103: 
104: 
105: def mean_cents(values: Sequence[int]) -> int:
106:     """Mean of integer cents rounded half up (ties away from zero)."""
107:     if not values:
108:         raise ValueError("mean_cents requires at least one value")
109:     return round_half_up(sum(values), len(values))
110: 
111: 
112: def profile_metrics(rows: Sequence[RowCents]) -> Metrics:
113:     """Compute I, F, S, B, H plus the F decomposition for one account.
114: 
115:     rows are the account's monthly rows; they are re sorted by month
116:     ascending inside so the last 6 row buffer window is exact no matter
117:     what order the caller passes.
118:     """
119:     if not rows:
120:         raise ValueError("profile_metrics requires at least one row")
121:     ordered = sorted(rows, key=lambda row: row.month)
122: 
123:     income = median_cents([row.money_in for row in ordered])
124:     spending = median_cents([row.money_out for row in ordered])
125:     fixed = median_cents(
126:         [
127:             row.household_bills + row.insurance + row.loan_payments
128:             for row in ordered
129:         ]
130:     )
131:     household = median_cents([row.household_bills for row in ordered])
132:     insurance = median_cents([row.insurance for row in ordered])
133:     loan_payments = median_cents([row.loan_payments for row in ordered])
134:     pension_total = sum(row.pension_in for row in ordered)
135:     window = ordered[-min(BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS, len(ordered)):]
136:     buffer_cents = mean_cents([row.avg_daily_balance for row in window])
137:     gap = spending - income
138: 
139:     return Metrics(
140:         income_cents=income,
141:         fixed_costs_cents=fixed,
142:         spending_cents=spending,
143:         buffer_cents=buffer_cents,
144:         household_bills_cents=household,
145:         insurance_cents=insurance,
146:         loan_payments_median_cents=loan_payments,
147:         pension_in_cents=pension_total,
148:         gap_cents=gap,
149:     )
150: 
151: 
152: def derive_flags(
153:     metric: Metrics, row_count: int, loan_status: str | None
154: ) -> dict[str, bool]:
155:     """Derive the five edge flags from metrics, history, and loan status.
156: 
157:     * pensioner: pension money in summed over all rows is above zero
158:     * thin_history: fewer than 18 monthly rows (a quarter of the 72
159:       month dataset span; the B window itself still averages min(6, n)
160:       rows regardless of this flag)
161:     * zero_income: median income I is exactly zero
162:     * defaulted_loan: the account has a loan with status D
163:     * negative_buffer: buffer B is below zero
164:     """
165:     return {
166:         "pensioner": metric.pension_in_cents > 0,
167:         "thin_history": row_count < THIN_HISTORY_ROWS,
168:         "zero_income": metric.income_cents == 0,
169:         "defaulted_loan": loan_status is not None and loan_status == DEFAULTED_STATUS,
170:         "negative_buffer": metric.buffer_cents < 0,
171:     }
172: 
173: 
174: def loan_payment_cents(monthly_payment_cents: int, status: str) -> int:
175:     """P: the loan payment when the loan runs at the end of 2025, else 0."""
176:     if status in RUNNING_STATUS_RULE:
177:         return monthly_payment_cents
178:     return 0

1: """Pure judge metrics over integer cent row sequences.
2: 
3: Every function in this module is pure: no pandas, no numpy, no file IO.
4: All money values are integer CAD cents and rounding happens once at the
5: metric boundary with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero).
6: 
7: Judge definitions from docs/tangerine-challenge.md:
8: 
9: * I = median of money_in over all monthly rows
10: * F = median over months of the per month row sum household_bills +
11:   insurance + loan_payments (per row sums first, never a sum of medians)
12: * S = median of money_out over all monthly rows
13: * B = mean of avg_daily_balance over the last min(6, n) rows sorted by
14:   month, rounded half up; fewer than 6 rows uses every available row
15: * H = median of household_bills over all monthly rows
16: * P = monthly_payment from loans.csv when status is C or D (running at
17:   the end of 2025), otherwise 0; P comes from the loan record in build.py
18: * gap = S minus I
19: 
20: Run from the repository root:
21: 
22:     uv run python -m scripts.engine.build
23: """
24: 
25: from __future__ import annotations
26: 
27: from dataclasses import dataclass
28: from typing import Sequence
29: 
30: # Rule versions recorded in the artifact meta.
31: METRIC_RULE_VERSION: str = "judge-metrics-v1"
32: 
33: # The buffer window is the last 6 rows by month (the judge rule for B).
34: BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS: int = 6
35: 
36: # The thin_history flag threshold: fewer than 18 monthly rows, a quarter
37: # of the 72 month dataset span (2020-01 to 2025-12). Every real account
38: # has at least 12 rows, so a 6 row threshold would never fire; 18 fires
39: # on the genuinely short histories (rationale recorded in the Phase E1
40: # decision record, docs/decisions.md). The flag is separate from
41: # BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS, which only decides how many rows B averages.
42: THIN_HISTORY_ROWS: int = 18
43: 
44: # The single swappable rule deciding which loan statuses count as running
45: # at the end of 2025 (user confirmed decision, docs/decisions.md E1).
46: RUNNING_STATUS_RULE: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"C", "D"})
47: DEFAULTED_STATUS: str = "D"
48: END_OF_2025_MONTH: str = "2025-12"
49: 
50: 
51: @dataclass(frozen=True)
52: class RowCents:
53:     """One monthly_summary row with every money value in integer cents."""
54: 
55:     month: str
56:     money_in: int
57:     money_out: int
58:     household_bills: int
59:     insurance: int
60:     loan_payments: int
61:     pension_in: int
62:     avg_daily_balance: int
63: 
64: 
65: @dataclass(frozen=True)
66: class Metrics:
67:     """The six judge numbers plus the F decomposition and the gap."""
68: 
69:     income_cents: int
70:     fixed_costs_cents: int
71:     spending_cents: int
72:     buffer_cents: int
73:     household_bills_cents: int
74:     insurance_cents: int
75:     loan_payments_median_cents: int
76:     pension_in_cents: int
77:     gap_cents: int
78: 
79: 
80: def round_half_up(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> int:
81:     """Divide with ROUND_HALF_UP: ties away from zero (decimal semantics).
82: 
83:     The positive case is (numerator + denominator // 2) // denominator;
84:     the sign split makes negative operands round away from zero on ties
85:     as well, which matches Python's decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.
86:     """
87:     if denominator <= 0:
88:         raise ValueError(f"denominator must be positive, got {denominator}")
89:     sign = 1 if numerator >= 0 else -1
90:     magnitude = (abs(numerator) + denominator // 2) // denominator
91:     return sign * magnitude
92: 
93: 
94: def median_cents(values: Sequence[int]) -> int:
95:     """Median of integer cents: middle value, or half up mean of two middles."""
96:     if not values:
97:         raise ValueError("median_cents requires at least one value")
98:     ordered = sorted(values)
99:     middle = len(ordered) // 2
100:     if len(ordered) % 2 == 1:
101:         return ordered[middle]
102:     return round_half_up(ordered[middle - 1] + ordered[middle], 2)
103: 
104: 
105: def mean_cents(values: Sequence[int]) -> int:
106:     """Mean of integer cents rounded half up (ties away from zero)."""
107:     if not values:
108:         raise ValueError("mean_cents requires at least one value")
109:     return round_half_up(sum(values), len(values))
110: 
111: 
112: def profile_metrics(rows: Sequence[RowCents]) -> Metrics:
113:     """Compute I, F, S, B, H plus the F decomposition for one account.
114: 
115:     rows are the account's monthly rows; they are re sorted by month
116:     ascending inside so the last 6 row buffer window is exact no matter
117:     what order the caller passes.
118:     """
119:     if not rows:
120:         raise ValueError("profile_metrics requires at least one row")
121:     ordered = sorted(rows, key=lambda row: row.month)
122: 
123:     income = median_cents([row.money_in for row in ordered])
124:     spending = median_cents([row.money_out for row in ordered])
125:     fixed = median_cents(
126:         [
127:             row.household_bills + row.insurance + row.loan_payments
128:             for row in ordered
129:         ]
130:     )
131:     household = median_cents([row.household_bills for row in ordered])
132:     insurance = median_cents([row.insurance for row in ordered])
133:     loan_payments = median_cents([row.loan_payments for row in ordered])
134:     pension_total = sum(row.pension_in for row in ordered)
135:     window = ordered[-min(BUFFER_WINDOW_ROWS, len(ordered)):]
136:     buffer_cents = mean_cents([row.avg_daily_balance for row in window])
137:     gap = spending - income
138: 
139:     return Metrics(
140:         income_cents=income,
141:         fixed_costs_cents=fixed,
142:         spending_cents=spending,
143:         buffer_cents=buffer_cents,
144:         household_bills_cents=household,
145:         insurance_cents=insurance,
146:         loan_payments_median_cents=loan_payments,
147:         pension_in_cents=pension_total,
148:         gap_cents=gap,
149:     )
150: 
151: 
152: def derive_flags(
153:     metric: Metrics, row_count: int, loan_status: str | None
154: ) -> dict[str, bool]:
155:     """Derive the five edge flags from metrics, history, and loan status.
156: 
157:     * pensioner: pension money in summed over all rows is above zero
158:     * thin_history: fewer than 18 monthly rows (a quarter of the 72
159:       month dataset span; the B window itself still averages min(6, n)
160:       rows regardless of this flag)
161:     * zero_income: median income I is exactly zero
162:     * defaulted_loan: the account has a loan with status D
163:     * negative_buffer: buffer B is below zero
164:     """
165:     return {
166:         "pensioner": metric.pension_in_cents > 0,
167:         "thin_history": row_count < THIN_HISTORY_ROWS,
168:         "zero_income": metric.income_cents == 0,
169:         "defaulted_loan": loan_status is not None and loan_status == DEFAULTED_STATUS,
170:         "negative_buffer": metric.buffer_cents < 0,
171:     }
172: 
173: 
174: def loan_payment_cents(monthly_payment_cents: int, status: str) -> int:
175:     """P: the loan payment when the loan runs at the end of 2025, else 0."""
176:     if status in RUNNING_STATUS_RULE:
177:         return monthly_payment_cents
178:     return 0

72: /** Look a band up by id (never undefined for a shipped id). */
73: export function verdictBandById(id: VerdictBandId): VerdictBand {

83:  * itself: the two special states are decided before any threshold, so
84:  * buffer_depleted always reads Critical and no_shortfall always reads
85:  * Clear no matter what deci months carry.
86:  */
87: export function verdictBand(answer: RunwayAnswer): VerdictBand {
88:   if (answer.state === 'buffer_depleted') {
89:     return verdictBandById('critical')
90:   }
91:   if (answer.state === 'no_shortfall') {
92:     return verdictBandById('clear')
93:   }
94:   const deci = answer.deciMonths
95:   if (deci < 10) {

97:   }

100:   }
101:   if (deci < 60) {
102:     return verdictBandById('watch')
103:   }
104:   if (deci < 120) {

106:   }
107:   return verdictBandById('clear')

Good. Now I have a clear picture. Let me plan Stage 1.

## Stage 1: planMath.ts additions + unit goldens/invariants

Additions to planMath.ts:
1. `GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6` (beside GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3)
2. `GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6]`
3. `GoalMilestone {monthsOfSpending, amountCents, monthsToReach, isGoal, isStretch}` + `goalMilestones(incomeCents, spendingCents)`
4. `LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'`
5. `LeverEffect {incomeDeltaCents, spendingDeltaCents, bufferDeltaCents}` (all E4 levers: income 0, buffer 0, spending <= 0)
6. `Lever {id, label, caveat, effect}`
7. `LeverInputs {shockedIncomeCents, shockedSpendingCents, oneOffCents, bufferCents (profile.buffer_cents pre one-off), fixedCostsCents (F), loanPaymentCents (P), insuranceCents, typicalSpendingCents (S)}`
8. `LeverStep {lever, incomeAfterCents, spendingAfterCents, bufferLeftCents, runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer, plusDeciMonths, stepDeciMonths}`
9. `LeverLadder {baseline, steps}`10. `leverLadder(input)`

Semantics:
- Order: shop_insurance → trim_discretionary → defer_loan
- Availability:
  - shop_insurance: insuranceCents > 0, spendingDelta = -insuranceCents
  - trim_discretionary: disc = max(0, S - (F+P)) > 0, spendingDelta = -disc
  - defer_loan: loanPaymentCents > 0, spendingDelta = -loanPaymentCents
- Composition: filter available levers in order, apply cumulatively: spendingAfter = max(0, shockedSpending + Σ deltas), defensive guard asserted unreachable on fixtures.
- Per step: re-run shocks.runway(bufferCents, oneOffCents, shockedIncome, spendingAfter)

```ts
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)

  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)

  const discretionary = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))
  const candidates: Lever[] = []
  if (insurance > 0) candidates.push(leverShopInsurance(insurance))
  if (discretionary > 0) candidates.push(leverTrimDiscretionary(discretionary))
  if (loan > 0) candidates.push(leverDeferLoan(loan))

  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
  let spending = shockedSpending
  let previous = baseline
  for (const lever of candidates) {
    spending = Math.max(0, spending + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
    const after = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spending)
    steps.push({
      lever,
      incomeAfterCents: income,
      spendingAfterCents: spending,
      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
      runwayAfter: after,
      plusDeciMonths: after.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
      stepDeciMonths: after.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
    })
    previous = after
  }

  return { baseline, steps }
}
```

export const GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6
export const GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS: readonly number[] = [1, 2, 3, 6]

export interface GoalMilestone {
  monthsOfSpending: number
  amountCents: number
  monthsToReach: number
  isGoal: boolean
  isStretch: boolean
}

export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[] {
  const income = cents(incomeCents)
  const spending = cents(spendingCents)
  const floorCents = scaleCents(income, GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT)
  const contributionCents = Math.max(income - spending, floorCents)
  return GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS.map((monthsOfSpending) => {
    const amountCents = monthsOfSpending * spending
    const monthsToReach =
      contributionCents <= 0
        ? MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
        : Math.floor((amountCents + contributionCents - 1) / contributionCents)
    return {
      monthsOfSpending,
      amountCents,
      monthsToReach,
      isGoal: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS,
      isStretch: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS,
    }
  })
}

export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)

  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)

  const discretionary = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))
  const candidates: Lever[] = []
  if (insurance > 0) candidates.push(leverShopInsurance(insurance))
  if (discretionary > 0) candidates.push(leverTrimDiscretionary(discretionary))
  if (loan > 0) candidates.push(leverDeferLoan(loan))

  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
  let spending = shockedSpending
  let previous = baseline
  for (const lever of candidates) {
    spending = Math.max(0, spending + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
    const after = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spending)
    steps.push({
      lever,
      incomeAfterCents: income,
      spendingAfterCents: spending,
      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
      runwayAfter: after,
      plusDeciMonths: after.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
      stepDeciMonths: after.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
    })
    previous = after
  }

  return { baseline, steps }
}
```

export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[] {
  const income = cents(incomeCents)
  const spending = cents(spendingCents)
  const floorCents = scaleCents(income, GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT)
  const contributionCents = Math.max(income - spending, floorCents)

  return GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS.map((monthsOfSpending) => {
    const amountCents = monthsOfSpending * spending
    const monthsToReach =
      contributionCents <= 0
        ? MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
        : Math.floor((amountCents + contributionCents - 1) / contributionCents)
    return {
      monthsOfSpending,
      amountCents,
      monthsToReach,
      isGoal: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS,
      isStretch: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS,
    }
  })
}
```

```ts
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)

  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)
  const discretionaryCents = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))

  const available: Lever[] = []
  if (insurance > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'shop_insurance',
      label: 'Shop insurance',
      caveat: SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -insurance, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (discretionaryCents > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'trim_discretionary',
      label: 'Trim discretionary',
      caveat: TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -discretionaryCents, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (loan > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'defer_loan',
      label: 'Defer loan',
      caveat: DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -loan, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }

  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
  let spendingAfterCents = shockedSpending
  let previous = baseline
  for (const lever of available) {
    spendingAfterCents = Math.max(0, spendingAfterCents + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
    const runwayAfter = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spendingAfterCents)
    steps.push({
      lever,
      incomeAfterCents: income,
      spendingAfterCents,
      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
      runwayAfter,
      plusDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
      stepDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
    })
    previous = runwayAfter
  }

  return { baseline, steps }
}

export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[] {
  const income = cents(incomeCents)
  const spending = cents(spendingCents)
  const floorCents = scaleCents(income, GOAL_CONTRIBUTION_FLOOR_PCT)
  const contributionCents = Math.max(income - spending, floorCents)

  return GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS.map((monthsOfSpending) => {
    const amountCents = monthsOfSpending * spending
    const monthsToReach =
      contributionCents <= 0
        ? MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
        : Math.floor((amountCents + contributionCents - 1) / contributionCents)
    return {
      monthsOfSpending,
      amountCents,
      monthsToReach,
      isGoal: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS,
      isStretch: monthsOfSpending === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS,
    }
  })
}
```

```ts
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)

  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)
  const discretionaryCents = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))

  const available: Lever[] = []
  if (insurance > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'shop_insurance',
      label: 'Shop insurance',
      caveat: SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -insurance, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (discretionaryCents > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'trim_discretionary',
      label: 'Trim discretionary',
      caveat: TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -discretionaryCents, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (loan > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'defer_loan',
      label: 'Defer loan',
      caveat: DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -loan, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }

  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
  let spendingAfterCents = shockedSpending
  let previous = baseline
  for (const lever of available) {
    spendingAfterCents = Math.max(0, spendingAfterCents + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
    const runwayAfter = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spendingAfterCents)
    steps.push({
      lever,
      incomeAfterCents: income,
      spendingAfterCents,
      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
      runwayAfter,
      plusDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
      stepDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
    })
    previous = runwayAfter
  }

  return { baseline, steps }
}
```

export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)

  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)
  const discretionaryCents = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))

  const available: Lever[] = []
  if (insurance > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'shop_insurance',
      label: 'Shop insurance',
      caveat: SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -insurance, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (discretionaryCents > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'trim_discretionary',
      label: 'Trim discretionary',
      caveat: TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -discretionaryCents, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }
  if (loan > 0) {
    available.push({
      id: 'defer_loan',
      label: 'Defer loan',
      caveat: DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT,
      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -loan, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
    })
  }

  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
  let spendingAfterCents = shockedSpending
  let previous = baseline
  for (const lever of available) {
    spendingAfterCents = Math.max(0, spendingAfterCents + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
    const runwayAfter = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spendingAfterCents)
    steps.push({
      lever,
      incomeAfterCents: income,
      spendingAfterCents,
      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
      runwayAfter,
      plusDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
      stepDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
    })
    previous = runwayAfter
  }

  return { baseline, steps }
}
```

+/**
+ * Backup levers (E4): an ordered, cumulative ladder of counterfactual
+ * cuts, each one sized from profile numbers (judge part 1 metrics), never
+ * from shocked ones. The three levers run free moves first: shop
+ * insurance, trim discretionary spending above the F plus P floor, then
+ * defer the loan payment. Every lever keeps income and the buffer
+ * untouched, so a step only ever reduces spending, and every +N months
+ * figure is the difference of two shocks.runway answers (this module
+ * never re-derives a runway any other way).
+ */

+

+  /** E4 levers never move income, so this is always 0 cents. */
+  incomeDeltaCents: number

+  spendingDeltaCents: number
+  /** E4 levers never touch the buffer, so this is always 0 cents. */

+  /** Median insurance cost in integer cents (profile metric, 0 when none). */
+  insuranceCents: number
+  /** S, typical monthly spending in integer cents (profile metric). */
+  typicalSpendingCents: number
+}

+export interface LeverStep {
+  lever: Lever
+  /** Shocked income plus the lever income delta (always shocked income). */
+  incomeAfterCents: number
+  /** Shocked spending plus every delta so far, floored at 0. */
+  spendingAfterCents: number
+  /** B minus the one off cost, unchanged by any E4 lever. */
+  bufferLeftCents: number
+  /** shocks.runway re run over this step's numbers. */
+  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer
+  /** Runway gain versus the baseline in tenths, never negative. */
+  plusDeciMonths: number
+  /** Runway gain versus the previous step in tenths, never negative. */
+  stepDeciMonths: number
+}

+  /** The shocked runway before any lever, equal to result.runway. */
+  baseline: RunwayAnswer
+  /** Available levers in ladder order, applied cumulatively. */
+  steps: LeverStep[]

+const SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT =

+const TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT =
+  'simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed'
+const DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT =
+  'simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled'
+
+/**
+ * Build the lever ladder for one shocked account. Levers appear in
+ * ladder order (insurance, discretionary trim, loan deferral) only when
+ * their profile input allows them, spending is recomputed with a
+ * defensive floor of 0 after each cumulative delta, and each step re
+ * runs shocks.runway over the same buffer, one off cost, and income.
+ */
+export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
+  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
+  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
+  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
+  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
+  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
+  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
+  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
+  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)
+
+  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)
+  const discretionaryCents = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))
+
+  const available: Lever[] = []
+  if (insurance > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'shop_insurance',
+      label: 'Shop insurance',
+      caveat: SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -insurance, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+  if (discretionaryCents > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'trim_discretionary',
+      label: 'Trim discretionary',
+      caveat: TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -discretionaryCents, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+  if (loan > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'defer_loan',
+      label: 'Defer loan',
+      caveat: DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -loan, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+
+  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
+  let spendingAfterCents = shockedSpending
+  let previous = baseline
+  for (const lever of available) {
+    spendingAfterCents = Math.max(0, spendingAfterCents + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
+    const runwayAfter = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spendingAfterCents)
+    steps.push({
+      lever,
+      incomeAfterCents: income,
+      spendingAfterCents,
+      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
+      runwayAfter,
+      plusDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
+      stepDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
+    })
+    previous = runwayAfter
+  }
+
+  return { baseline, steps }
+}

+  /** One off cost already subtracted from the buffer by the twist. */
+  oneOffCents: number
+  /** profile.buffer_cents before the one off cost, the runway's B. */
+  bufferCents: number
+  /** F, typical fixed costs in integer cents (profile metric). */
+  fixedCostsCents: number
+  /** P, the running loan payment in integer cents (profile metric). */
+  loanPaymentCents: number
+  /** Median insurance cost in integer cents (profile metric, 0 when none). */
+  insuranceCents: number
+  /** S, typical monthly spending in integer cents (profile metric). */
+  typicalSpendingCents: number
+}
+
+export interface LeverStep {
+  lever: Lever
+  /** Shocked income plus the lever income delta (always shocked income). */
+  incomeAfterCents: number
+  /** Shocked spending plus every delta so far, floored at 0. */
+  spendingAfterCents: number
+  /** B minus the one off cost, unchanged by any E4 lever. */
+  bufferLeftCents: number
+  /** shocks.runway re run over this step's numbers. */
+  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer
+  /** Runway gain versus the baseline in tenths, never negative. */
+  plusDeciMonths: number
+  /** Runway gain versus the previous step in tenths, never negative. */
+  stepDeciMonths: number
+}
+
+export interface LeverLadder {
+  /** The shocked runway before any lever, equal to result.runway. */
+  baseline: RunwayAnswer
+  /** Available levers in ladder order, applied cumulatively. */
+  steps: LeverStep[]
+}
+
+const SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT =
+  'simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation'
+const TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT =
+  'simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed'
+const DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT =
+  'simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled'
+
+/**
+ * Build the lever ladder for one shocked account. Levers appear in
+ * ladder order (insurance, discretionary trim, loan deferral) only when
+ * their profile input allows them, spending is recomputed with a
+ * defensive floor of 0 after each cumulative delta, and each step re
+ * runs shocks.runway over the same buffer, one off cost, and income.
+ */
+export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder {
+  const income = cents(input.shockedIncomeCents)
+  const shockedSpending = cents(input.shockedSpendingCents)
+  const oneOff = cents(input.oneOffCents)
+  const buffer = cents(input.bufferCents)
+  const fixed = cents(input.fixedCostsCents)
+  const loan = cents(input.loanPaymentCents)
+  const insurance = cents(input.insuranceCents)
+  const typical = cents(input.typicalSpendingCents)
+
+  const baseline = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, shockedSpending)
+  const discretionaryCents = Math.max(0, typical - (fixed + loan))
+
+  const available: Lever[] = []
+  if (insurance > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'shop_insurance',
+      label: 'Shop insurance',
+      caveat: SHOP_INSURANCE_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -insurance, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+  if (discretionaryCents > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'trim_discretionary',
+      label: 'Trim discretionary',
+      caveat: TRIM_DISCRETIONARY_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -discretionaryCents, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+  if (loan > 0) {
+    available.push({
+      id: 'defer_loan',
+      label: 'Defer loan',
+      caveat: DEFER_LOAN_CAVEAT,
+      effect: { incomeDeltaCents: 0, spendingDeltaCents: -loan, bufferDeltaCents: 0 },
+    })
+  }
+
+  const steps: LeverStep[] = []
+  let spendingAfterCents = shockedSpending
+  let previous = baseline
+  for (const lever of available) {
+    spendingAfterCents = Math.max(0, spendingAfterCents + lever.effect.spendingDeltaCents)
+    const runwayAfter = runway(buffer, oneOff, income, spendingAfterCents)
+    steps.push({
+      lever,
+      incomeAfterCents: income,
+      spendingAfterCents,
+      bufferLeftCents: buffer - oneOff,
+      runwayAfter,
+      plusDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - baseline.deciMonths,
+      stepDeciMonths: runwayAfter.deciMonths - previous.deciMonths,
+    })
+    previous = runwayAfter
+  }
+
+  return { baseline, steps }
+}
